criteria.quote: Grab one tail. A millennium-long curse may follow.
criteria.revision: Make the evidence source and the family-scale implication part of the first beat: "Ninetales' Pokédex lore says grabbing one tail could bring a 1,000-year curse—and another entry says descendants can be cursed too."

criteria.quote: The Pokédex calls Ninetales smart, vengeful, and hard to cross.
criteria.revision: Replace the generic phrase "hard to cross" and the unsupported caption "NINETALES DOES NOT FORGET" with the exact characterization: "The Pokédex calls Ninetales very smart and very vengeful."

criteria.quote: Why would touching one tail threaten a family for a millennium?
criteria.revision: Make the open question about the two pieces of lore rather than inventing a cause: "Does grabbing the tail cause the family curse—or are these separate parts of Ninetales' legend?"

Stop repeating the curse's duration across the first four scenes. Progress from the grab, to the descendant clause, then introduce a new layer: "But Ninetales' tails are not ordinary—each is said to carry supernatural power."

criteria.quote: One entry says the curse reaches the offender's descendants too.
criteria.revision: Delay this reveal until after the audience hears that grabbing one tail may curse the offender, then land the exact escalation: "And Ultra Sun makes the punishment even bigger: those who cross Ninetales are said to be cursed for 1,000 years, along with their descendants."

criteria.quote: The Pokédex says that curse lasts one thousand years.
criteria.revision: Replace this restatement with a distinct mythological detail: "The curse is only one part of the legend: other entries say nine saints—or nine wizards—were united into Ninetales."

criteria.quote: Ninetales' Pokédex lore links its supernatural tails to a curse lasting 1,000 years and reaching descendants.
criteria.revision: End by separating what the lore confirms from what it leaves unknown: "The entries give the curse a terrifying scope—1,000 years and possibly descendants—but never explain what the curse actually does."

criteria.quote: Is Ninetales' curse brilliant lore, or too harsh?
criteria.revision: Make the split more specific to the evidence: "Does including the offender's descendants make Ninetales' curse more compelling—or does it cross the line into excessive punishment?"
